Trample + deathtouch forced with a real Lure (the SIM does not voluntarily block an attacker with deathtouch; Lure forces it by rule, like must-block): land + RAW cheat (no auto-pass) — Elvish Warrior 2/3 to the battlefield + 8 Forests + Lure/Rancor/Basilisk Collar in hand — + casts Lure→Rancor→Collar ({1}{G}{G}+{G}+{2}, tapping Forests) + equipping the Collar (equip {2}) + attacking with the 4/3 Warrior (Rancor +2/+0 grants trample; Collar grants deathtouch+lifelink) confirming with the special button. Timing finding (re-validated in 1.4.62): seeding the Grizzly at the start (800 ms after the first cheat) no longer works (the game advances ~2 turns/s, the Grizzly dies or hits us before the combo is assembled and the life does not add up); the Grizzly is seeded once on the turn of the attack, gated by Lure+Rancor+Collar attached, and the driver attacks as soon as there is a fresh Grizzly. Finding that corrects the plan: a 4/2 attacker (Grizzly+Rancor) dies to the blocking damage, which is simultaneous (deathtouch does not "hit first"); with Elvish Warrior 2/3 the attacker is 4/3 and survives with 2 damage. The damage assignment arrives as GAME_GET_MULTI_AMOUNT (items[min/max/defaultValue]; the server's defaultValue already reduces the lethal to 1 because of deathtouch) and the default is answered (1 to the blocker): the engine computes the trample excess (damage - assigned = 3) and sends it to the player. Capture: SIM's Grizzly in the graveyard (deathtouch lethal), SIM life 20→17 (1 lethal + 3 trample), our life 20→24 (lifelink 4 from the 4 damage; 22 is no longer accepted: without stray Grizzlies the SIM does not get to hit before the attack) and Elvish Warrior 4/3 alive on the battlefield with damage=2, rules ["Trample","Deathtouch","Lifelink"], Lure+Rancor+Collar attached. trample-deathtouch driver with cheatSetup + real Lure.

Evidence in the view: the SIM's permanent with cardTypes PLANESWALKER and `loyalty` "3" (a string derived from the LOYALTY counter, also in counters [{name:"loyalty",count:3}]) and gv.combat[] with defenderId = the PW's UUID and the Grizzly in attackers. attack-pw driver with cheatSetup.

Propaganda ({2}{U}, "Creatures can't attack you or a planeswalker you control unless their controller pays {2} for each of those creatures.") cheated onto the SIM's battlefield; our own cheated Grizzly Bears (no summoning sickness) attacks and a Treasure token (created by a real Prosperous Innkeeper cast with a Forest) is sacrificed to cover part of the cost (the rest is paid with a Forest). Hexproof without ward via cheatSetup (the missing case): Slippery Bogle ({G/U} 1/1, HexproofAbility, no ETB) onto the opponent's battlefield and our own Lightning Bolt. Coin + d20 via cheatSetup: Tavern Swindler ({1}{B} 2/2) cheated onto the battlefield (no summoning sickness; casting it would leave it summoning-sick and it could not activate {T} this turn) activates "{T}, Pay 3 life: Flip a coin. REAL fail-to-find via cheatSetup: Evolving Wilds onto the battlefield + activation "{T}, Sacrifice: Search your library for a basic land card" and the GAME_TARGET is declined with sendPlayerBoolean(false). Path: TargetCardInLibrary is born required=false when the filter has predicates (setRequired(!filter.hasPredicates()); FILTER_CARD_BASIC_LAND adds SuperType.BASIC, rule 701.15b), so HumanPlayer.chooseTarget breaks the loop ("done or cancel" → break) and searchLibrary returns false; Demonic Tutor (FILTER_CARD with no predicates) is required=true and that is why declining re-asked in a loop. The GAME_TARGET arrives with message "Select a basic land card", flag=false (= required: GameClientMessage.flag) and options.possibleTargets with the library's 53 lands — that flag=false is what the web needs to offer the "fail to find" (today it does not use it). Swing has no special button: the FeedbackPanel's right button sends the same sendPlayerBoolean(false) (text "Done" from options[UI.right.btn.text] when min targets are already met). Capture: Evolving Wilds in the graveyard, only 1 land on the battlefield (the one played from hand; if it failed the other way there would be 2), libraryCount untouched (53 in the frame: 60-7, no draw; 52 if the SIM starts) and empty stack. fail-to-find driver with cheatSetup.

" and the raw marker "ICON_REQUIREMust attack (...)". The requirement applies while the permanent is on the battlefield (attacking or not), so the icon is in the same frame as the attack. Evidence in the frame: the SIM's Recluse in gv.combat[].attackers (tapped:true) and its restriction cardIcon in the battlefield's CardView. always-attack driver with cheatSetup.

Battle Invasion of Gobakhan ({1}{W}, Battle — Siege, startingDefense 3) cheated onto OUR battlefield next to a 2/2 Grizzly Bears in a single cheatSetup (same player) and attacked by the Grizzly on the same turn as the cheat (T1 if the human starts, T2 if the SIM starts; in the final capture T2). Finding: the battle must be OUR OWN, not the SIM's — Combat.setDefenders (Combat.java:1389-1393) uses FilterBattlePermanent + ProtectedByOpponentPredicate (a legal defender for P only if its protector ∈ opponents(P)); with the SIM's battle the protector is the human and the human cannot attack it, with our own the protector is the SIM (PermanentImpl.chooseProtector, automatic in a duel) and it can ("You and others can attack it"). The direct battlefield cheat does not fire an ETB (CardUtil.putCardOntoBattlefieldWithEffects "without ETB") but goes through PermanentImpl.entersBattlefield: it adds the DEFENSE counters (3) and chooses a protector. Defender choice: when declaring the Grizzly with 2 defenders (SIM player + battle) the GAME_TARGET "Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack" arrives (HumanPlayer.selectDefender, TargetDefender/FilterDefender) whose observed payload is data.targets=[SIM player UUID, battle UUID] (2 options), min/max 0 and options.queryType "PICK_TARGET"; it is answered with sendPlayerUUID(battleId) + sendPlayerBoolean(false) to confirm (never special with 2+ defenders). Evidence in the view: step COMBAT_DAMAGE, our permanent with cardTypes BATTLE and `defense` "1" (3→1 from the Grizzly's 2; also counters [{name:"defense",count:1}], PermanentImpl.damage 1192-1199) and gv.combat[] with defenderId = the battle's UUID, defenderName "Invasion of Gobakhan" and the Grizzly in attackers, empty stack; the battle's rules includes "Protected by <sim>" (the protector's addInfo). attack-battle driver with cheatSetup.

Floating mana and confirmEmptyManaPool: on the first turn of ours, clicking the Forest played (sendPlayerUUID of the permanent = activates its only mana ability) leaves {G} in the pool; when passing priority (sendPlayerBoolean false) HumanPlayer.passWithManaPoolCheck fires the GAME_ASK chooseUse "You still have mana in your mana pool and it will be lost. Pass anyway?" (only with userData.confirmEmptyManaPool=true, which is the proxy's default: UserData.getDefaultUserDataView; the web forwards it in GAME_INIT with updatePreferences {confirmEmptyManaPool} and toggles it in GameMenu → settings.manaPayment.confirmEmptyPool) and it is answered true = continue. The captured frame is the GAME_UPDATE_AND_INFORM immediately after answering the ASK: me.manaPool.green=1 (not yet emptied), empty stack, tapped Forest and priority already yielded to the SIM (hasPriority=false, isActive=true) — the ASK arrives as GAME_ASK (not as GAME_UPDATE) and rec-lib only captures GAME_UPDATE, so this is the state closest to the warning (the driver's fallback re-floats on a later turn if the pool were emptied before capturing). ","It's currently day/night, active player has cast N spells this turn. CONCEDE in the 1st mulligan window (GAME_ASK "Mulligan down to 6 cards?"): the server DOES honor it — GameImpl.setConcedingPlayer uses state.getChoosingPlayerId() (set by Mulligan.executeMulliganPhase), HumanPlayer.signalPlayerConcede(true) wakes waitForResponse and checkConcede→leave→end leave an immediate GAME_UPDATE with players[].hasLeft=true (turn 1, hand 0, no lands played, opponent with 7). The CONCEDE is processed before the keep/mulligan answer the driver sends (a mulligan true was sent and the dialog was already cut). Uruk-hai Berserker (LTR 112, {2}{B} 3/2; ETB "the Ring tempts you") + 2×Ranger's Firebrand (LTR 143, {R} sorcery: 2 damage to any target — GAME_TARGET "Select any target" with 3 legal UUIDs, the SIM's is chosen — and "the Ring tempts you") cast for real via cheatSetup (cards to hand + 2 Swamps/2 Mountains on the battlefield; mana paid with the requested color in GAME_PLAY_MANA: {2}{B}→Swamp, {R}→Mountain) against the passive SIM: level 1 → 2 → 3 on T1. CONTRACT (finding): the Ring has NO level or bearer as its own fields. The level is DERIVED from players[].commandList → EmblemView "The Ring" with `rules` (one line per ability added by TheRingEmblem.addNextAbility: level 1 = static legendary+evasion in ONE rule, levels 2/3/4 = triggers; the web does level = min(4, max(1, rules.length)), MechanicsTray.tsx). Frame invariant: The Ring in commandList with rules.length=3, cardIcons RINGBEARER on the Berserker, 2 Firebrands in the graveyard and empty stack. the-ring driver with cheatSetup.

Real choice of who starts with the opt-out skipStartingPlayerChoice:false (without the fork's deterministic shortcut, rec-lib forwards it in createTable): GameImpl.init does the random toss (pickChoosingPlayer, inform "won the toss") and ONLY the toss winner receives the prompt — ONE player, not both. Exact prompt payload: GAME_TARGET with message "Select a starting player" and targets=[simPlayerId, myPlayerId], options={queryType:"PICK_TARGET", chosenTargets:[]}, flag=true; it is answered with sendPlayerUUID of the chosen playerId (same path as runTournamentRecorder for /starting player/i). Nothing reaches the opponent: if the SIM wins the toss, its ComputerPlayer.makeChoice compares target.getMessage(game)=="Select a starting player" and picks itself without asking (the run does not capture and retries; ~50% toss). Timeout: GameController.startResponseIdleTimeout(choosingPlayerId) keeps running until the chosen one answers. After the choice the server emits sendStartMessage ("X chooses that Y will start") only as an inform in the log. Capture of the following state: turn 1, we are active (we picked ourselves) with gv.activePlayerId == me.playerId, land played (Forest) and empty stack. starting-player driver.

Gideon of the Trials (AKH 14, {1}{W}{W}, loyalty 3; AKH from Amonkhet.java "AKH") cast for real via cheatSetup (to hand + 3 Plains on the battlefield; mana paid with GAME_PLAY_MANA tapping one Plains per symbol) and its 0-loyalty ability that creates an emblem activated with a CLICK on the permanent (sendPlayerUUID of its battlefield id, NOT the ability's UUID — HumanPlayer.activateAbility resolves the picker: GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY with AbilityPickerView.choices = Map<UUID,String> "1. +1: ...", "2. 0: ...", "3. 0: You get an emblem with ..."; the label with "emblem" is chosen). Karn Liberated ({7}, loyalty 6) cheated directly onto the battlefield with cheatSetup (it enters with its 6 loyalty counters; with no "as it enters" decision the cheat is safe) against a passive SIM: +4 legal on T1 (6→10, GAME_CHOOSE_ABILITY with "+4: Target player exiles a card from their hand" answered by text; the GAME_TARGET "Select a player" is aimed at the SIM, which exiles a card from its hand) and +4 again (10→14); with exactly 14 loyalty the -14 is activated (readable by PayLoyaltyCost.canPay: loyalty + cost >= 0). The restart does NOT arrive as GAME_INIT nor as GAME_OVER: KarnLiberatedEffect.apply calls GameState.clearOnGameRestart() + Player.init/useDeck + game.start(null) INSIDE the -14's resolution, and the game re-initializes with the SAME gameId (the proxy sees no new GAME_INIT; rec-lib confirms it: only GAME_UPDATE). The first GAME_UPDATE of the restarted game brings turn 1, activePlayerId = Karn's controller, hands redealt by init (7/7 after the mulligan ASK, resolved by rec-lib's default), fresh libraries (me 53, SIM 93) and empty battlefield/graveyard/stack without Karn (shuffled back into the library); that frame is the capture. Finding of the engine's "dirty hack": the cards exiled with Karn in the old game are NOT re-placed on the battlefield in the first frame and their trail is inconsistent between runs (run 2: empty exiles; run 3: 1 SIM Forest still in exile) — the UI must not trust them. The UI must re-initialize with that GAME_UPDATE (not wait for GAME_INIT) and accept turn=1 after an advanced game. karn-restart driver with cheatSetup.

Game clock timeout. Table with timeLimit=MIN___5 (300s, the engine's real minimum — the web wizard only goes down to 15 min) via the standalone game-clock-timeout.mjs driver, because rec-lib.mjs does not expose timeLimit/bufferTime in its hardcoded createTable (a recording-tooling gap, not an engine one; rec-lib.mjs was not touched). The driver keeps its hand and then deliberately ignores every priority window: HumanPlayer.priority() keeps the clock running (game.resumeTimer) until it runs out → GameController→game.timerTimeout→PlayerImpl.timerTimeout (quit+timerTimeout+concede). Capture (turn 1, COMBAT/DECLARE_ATTACKERS): the controlled player with priorityTimeLeftSecs=0 and hasLeft=true but life=20 intact; the opponent with priorityTimeLeftSecs=300 untouched — the clock asymmetry is the proof of timeout, not concession/damage. The text 'run out of time' lives in the END_GAME_INFO callback (not in GAME_OVER, which this driver does capture) and was not recorded in this frame; the visible "low timer" warning already exists on the client via PlayerInfoBar.tsx isTimeLow at ≤30s (PlayerView.priorityTimeLeftSecs), verified by reading code but not in e2e.

Multikicker (Everflowing Chalice {0}, Multikicker {2}): the engine prompt is REPEATED and in chooseUse mode — "Pay 1 time {2} ?", "Pay 2 times {2} ?", … (KickerAbility.addOptionalAdditionalCosts; it is not GAME_CHOOSE_CHOICE nor a GAME_GET_AMOUNT). Strive (Launch the Fleet {W}, StriveAbility "{1}"): two of our Grizzly Bears cheated in + 3 Plains; the targets arrive as a repeated GAME_TARGET (declined with false when done) and the final cost is {1}{W} (paid with 2 Plains). Multiplayer combat with several defenders: a 4-player FFA (1 human + 3 SIM, `playerTypes`/`simDecks` from rec-lib) with one of our Grizzlies cheated in. FINDING 2026-09-17: the defender GAME_TARGET was not arriving because MatchOptions defaults to attackOption=LEFT (in FFA `Combat.getAttackablePlayers` leaves only 1 defender and HumanPlayer.selectDefender declares without asking); the table is now created with `attackOption: MULTIPLE` (a new passthrough in rec-lib.mjs). When declaring the attacker the engine asks for the defender (TargetDefender "Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack") and the driver picks the LAST SIM; the capture requires the combat group with defenderId = that SIM. It is the case the overlay preview (CombatArrowsOverlay, `players.find(p => p.playerId !== activePlayerId)`) does not cover in a pod: the replay asserts the real arrow via `[data-arrow-from]`/`[data-arrow-to]`.

A 4-player Commander FFA (1 human + 3 SIM) with a legal deck (99 Mountains + Krenko, Mob Boss). CONTRACT PROBE 2026-09-17: commander damage has NO field in the view (`PlayerView`/`GameView`/`CommanderView` do not expose it; it lives in the engine's `CommanderInfoWatcher.damageToPlayer`) — it travels ONLY as cardState info in the `rules` of the commander card/permanent ("Commander did N combat damage to player <name>."), which the web parses in `CommanderDamageMatrix.extractDamage`. Krenko is cast FROM THE COMMAND ZONE (cheating it would create another copy with a different id that the watcher does not see) with 8 cheated Mountains and attacks the LAST SIM with `attackOption: MULTIPLE` (the LEFT default does not generate a GAME_TARGET, see pod-combat); then our own Lightning Bolt sends it back to the command zone, which is where the CardView keeps the damage line (the matrix enumerates commanders from commandList, not from the battlefield). Capture: Krenko in commandList with the damage line and the last SIM's life 40−N.

A real 6-player FFA (1 human + 5 SIM) on a "Free For All" table: a stable frame on our first main phase with the land played (no cheat or combat). Evidence of the layout decision (only standard with switcher for 5+): the view brings 6 players and the replay requires `game-board` (NOT `pod-board`), a visible `.opponent-switcher-bar` and 6 `.opp-pill` pills — `effectiveBoardLayout` falls back to standard when totalPlayers > MAX_BOARD_PLAYERS=4.

Slicer, Hired Muscle (BOT 6/21, Transformers; DFC 3/4 double strike + haste) with cheatSetup onto our battlefield on T1: on the SIM's upkeep its trigger (BeginningOfUpkeepTriggeredAbility OPPONENT) asks the CONTROLLER "you may have that player gain control of Slicer until end of turn. If you do, untap Slicer, goad it, and it can't be sacrificed this turn. If you don't, convert it." and the driver answers YES (GAME_ASK chooseUse). Capture: Slicer on the SIM's battlefield (the view follows the real controller) untapped (tapped:false from the untap) and with the goad hint in `rules`/`cardIcons` (OTHER_HAS_RESTRICTIONS, "Goaded by <player> (must attack)" — same path as goad.json; `goadingPlayers` is not serialized). It tests the case "yield control of your permanent to the opponent on THEIR upkeep" (the reverse direction of Threaten) with no new contract fields.

Companion AVAILABLE (Lurrus of the Dream-Den in the sideboard; deck 24 Forests + 36 Grizzly Bears, MV ≤ 2 so the condition is legal). On initialization the engine asks "Use Lurrus … as your companion?" (chooseUse) and the driver answers YES; the companion stays in the companion zone (GameView.companion, RevealedView). The driver plays the turn's land + 2 Forests via cheatSetup and stops WITHOUT paying: it captures the first game view in which the card's id (key of canPlayObjects.objects) appears with a record of the playable buckets [usually `other`, CompanionAbility extends SpecialAction] — the exact shape that must enable the web viewer's click (issue #3). The record.id is the ability's id, DIFFERENT from the key: a client that compares the two never offers the action (a bug this frame pins). Capture: Lurrus still in the companion zone (NOT in hand), canPlayObjects.objects[id] with a non-empty bucket.

OPPONENT reveal (issue #1): the SIM plays Trinket Mage ({2}{U}; ETB searches for an artifact MV ≤ 1, reveals it and puts it into its hand) and the human (60 Forests, plays a land and passes) captures the game view with the opponent's `GameView.revealed` entry. To make the capture early and deterministic, cheatSetup puts a Trinket Mage in the SIM's hand and 3 Aether Vial in its library; Aether Vial is a noncreature artifact, so the SimPlayer never casts it and the search always finds one. It pins that the reveal from someone else's search reaches MY view (and therefore the web's `InfoWindows` viewer must paint it): the entry is named after the source card ("Trinket Mage …") and carries the revealed Aether Vial as a CardView.

The branch opposite to slicer.json of the same trigger (BeginningOfUpkeepTriggeredAbility OPPONENT): the driver answers NO to the chooseUse, so the engine converts Slicer to its back face instead of yielding it. The back face is "Slicer, High-Speed Antagonist", a Vehicle (ARTIFACT/VEHICLE) with living metal, and the engine publishes the CREATURE type CONDITIONALLY per turn: `["ARTIFACT"]` on the opponent's turn (this frame, turn 3) and `["ARTIFACT","CREATURE"]` on yours (slicer-living-metal.json, turn 4). It pins that `cardTypes` is a per-turn volatile value, not a stable property of the card: any board placement that depends on it moves the card around on every turn change. `attachedTo` is null in both: no attachment is involved.

Any-time top-card peek (Sphinx of Jwar Isle, ZEN 68, {4}{U}{U}) cast for real from hand on turn 1 after a land drop; Sphinx + 5 Islands arrive by cheatSetup (the deck is 60 Islands). Capture: the first view whose GameView.lookedAt carries a group named "Top card of your library" — the channel that feeds game/topCardPeek.ts and the slot beside the library. Contract note: that group is a LookedAtView, so its cards are SimpleCardView entries ({id, expansionSetCode, cardNumber, ...}), NOT CardView: no name, no rules text. The engine writes it once when LookAtTopCardOfLibraryAnyTimeEffect applies (PlayerImpl.lookAtCards -> fireUpdatePlayersEvent), guarded by canLookAtNextTopLibraryCard (no new peek while a spell is being paid for). Future Sight is NOT this channel in this fork (it is PlayWithTheTopCardRevealedEffect -> PlayerView.topCard, pinned by top-card-revealed.mjs).

Revealed top card (Future Sight, MH1 53, {2}{U}{U}{U}) cast for real from hand on turn 1 after a land drop; Future Sight + 4 Islands arrive by cheatSetup (the deck is 60 Islands). Capture: the first view whose controlled PlayerView carries a non-null topCard — PlayerView.java fills it from the CURRENT library top while the player is topCardRevealed, so it is a full CardView (name, rules, P/T), unlike the SimpleCardView payload of GameView.lookedAt. Read by board/crossZone.ts, board/boardShared.ts, board/targetZones.ts and the library chip of game/ResourceBar.tsx (which hides the peek slot when both channels point at the same card id).

WITH → WITHOUT → WITH triple of consecutive views around the "Top card of your library" lookedAt group (Sphinx of Jwar Isle cast for real, same setup as top-card-peek.json): proves the group alternates with empty views on the wire (effect pass re-adds it, lookAtCards clears it after sending), so the client is right to keep it as persistent library-side state instead of an event. Stale pin: each WITH group holds exactly one SimpleCardView pointer, and the id tracks the library (same libraryCount on both WITH ends → same id, changed library → changed id), so LookedAt.add never accumulates a stale card under the title.

First own PRECOMBAT_MAIN priority window with a land in hand and none on the battlefield. Proves the engine lists the land drop in canPlayObjects (basicPlayAbilities 'Play Mountain', one entry per hand land), so smart stops can trust the server instead of guessing from card names.

Untapped Sol Ring and Cascade Bluffs (filter land) with priority. Proves the engine files non-basic mana abilities under canPlayObjects `other` ("{T}: Add {C}{C}.", "{U/R}, {T}: Add {U}{U}."), not `basicManaAbilities`, so smart stops must recognise them by text or they count as a playable window.
